raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

On Intel XPU, `openbmb/MiniCPM-o-2_6` sometimes answers an image question with `!` repeated until the output limit. On POPE, 126 of 9000 answers came back like this. The affected questions change on every server restart, but stay the same within one server.

Cause:
- The Idefics2 vision encoder pads the image slices in a batch to one common length, `(bsz, seq_len)`. `cu_seqlens`, however, holds the real slice lengths.
- `VisionIntelXPUAttention` passed the padded `q/k/v` and those `cu_seqlens` to `flash_attn_varlen_func`.
- So every slice after a padded one attended over the wrong rows. The real rows past `cu_seqlens[-1]` were never written; the kernel output comes from `new_empty`, so they keep leftover memory.
- When that memory holds NaN, the logits become NaN and argmax returns token 0 (`!`).
- The encoded image is cached, so every question on that image fails until the server restarts.

## Modifications

- `VisionIntelXPUAttention.forward`: for `bsz > 1`, describe the padded layout to the kernel instead of the packed one: `cu_seqlens` at each image's padded offset (`seq_len` apart) and `seqused_q` / `seqused_k` with the real lengths. `max_seqlen` is the padded `seq_len`.
  - Each image attends only over its own real rows. The kernel skips the padding rows and returns them as zeros.
  - It is one kernel call over the padded tensor: no host sync, no boolean indexing, static shapes.
- `bsz == 1` (packed encoders such as Qwen-VL) is unchanged.
- New test `test_xpu_attn_padded_batch_attends_within_each_image` in `test/registered/xpu/test_vision_backend_selection.py`. It uses slice lengths 1036/1014/1014 and head_dim 72, from a failing MiniCPM-o batch. It fails on main and passes with this change.

**Depends on sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu#583**, which implements `seqused_q` / `seqused_k` in `flash_attn_varlen_func`. The pinned v0.4.0 accepts them but ignores them, so this PR needs a kernel release with sgl-kernel-xpu#583 and a pin bump before it can merge.

Note for reviewers: the `fa3`, `fa4` and `triton_attn` vision backends receive the same padded layout with packed `cu_seqlens`. CUDA FA3 can express it with `seqused_q` / `seqused_k`, which the `fa3` backend does not pass. This PR does not change them.

## Accuracy Tests

lmms_eval `pope` on `openbmb/MiniCPM-o-2_6`: full set (9000), seed 42, Intel Arc Pro B60, tp-size 2.

| | pope_accuracy | pope_f1_score | `!!!!` answers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| before | 86.84 | 87.29 | 126 |
| this PR (with sgl-kernel-xpu#583) | **88.14** | **87.37** | **0** |
| H200 reference (CUDA, tp-size 1) | 88.09 | 87.28 | 0 |

```bash
sglang serve --model-path openbmb/MiniCPM-o-2_6 --device xpu --tp-size 2 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.70 --trust-remote-code --enable-multimodal --attention-backend triton
python3 -m lmms_eval --model openai \
  --model_args model_version=openbmb/MiniCPM-o-2_6,num_concurrent=16 \
  --tasks pope --batch_size 16 --seed 42
```

Unit test on B60 with sgl-kernel-xpu#583: `pytest test/registered/xpu/test_vision_backend_selection.py`. On main: 1 failed, 4 passed. With this PR: 5 passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

One `VisionIntelXPUAttention` call on Arc Pro B60 with sgl-kernel-xpu#583 (16 heads, head_dim 72, bf16), in microseconds:

| batch | main | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 3 images, 1036/1014/1014 rows | 654 | 611 |
| 10 images, 1036 + 9 x 1014 rows | 1749 | 1735 |
| 13 unpadded images of 1025 rows | 3085 | 3072 |

The padded path no longer derives `max_seqlen` from `cu_seqlens` on the host, which removes one sync per encoder layer. POPE end to end took 12:14 (server ready to eval done).

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (N/A)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

files.patch:
@@ -1099,13 +1099,22 @@ def forward(
         cu_seqlens_source = cu_seqlens
         cu_seqlens = resolve_seqlens(cu_seqlens_source, bsz, seq_len, device=q.device)
         cu_seqlens = cu_seqlens.to(dtype=torch.int32).to(q.device)
-        max_seqlen = resolve_max_seqlen(cu_seqlens_source, cu_seqlens)
+        seqused = None
+        if bsz > 1 and cu_seqlens.numel() == bsz + 1:
+            # rows are padded per image to seq_len while cu_seqlens holds the real lengths
+            seqused = cu_seqlens[1:] - cu_seqlens[:-1]
+            cu_seqlens = _get_cu_seqlens_for_shape(bsz, seq_len, device=q.device)
+            max_seqlen = seq_len
+        else:
+            max_seqlen = resolve_max_seqlen(cu_seqlens_source, cu_seqlens)
 
         fa_kwargs = dict(
             cu_seqlens_q=cu_seqlens,
             cu_seqlens_k=cu_seqlens,
             max_seqlen_q=max_seqlen,
             max_seqlen_k=max_seqlen,
+            seqused_q=seqused,
+            seqused_k=seqused,
             softmax_scale=softmax_scale,
             window_size=window_size,
         )

@@ -1,7 +1,10 @@
+import itertools
 import sys
 from types import SimpleNamespace
 
 import pytest
+import torch
+import torch.nn.functional as F
 
 from sglang.srt.layers.attention import vision
 from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_xpu_ci
@@ -51,5 +54,31 @@ def test_xpu_backend_selection_priority(
     assert backend == expected
 
 
+def test_xpu_attn_padded_batch_attends_within_each_image():
+    """Images padded to a common seq_len with real lengths in cu_seqlens must each
+    attend only over their own rows, and the padding rows must come back zero."""
+    lens = [1036, 1014, 1014]
+    bsz, seq_len, heads, head_dim = len(lens), max(lens), 16, 72
+    cu_seqlens = torch.tensor(
+        [0, *itertools.accumulate(lens)], dtype=torch.int32, device="xpu"
+    )
+    q, k, v = (
+        torch.randn(bsz * seq_len, heads, head_dim, device="xpu", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        for _ in range(3)
+    )
+
+    out = vision.VisionIntelXPUAttention().forward(
+        q=q, k=k, v=v, cu_seqlens=cu_seqlens, bsz=bsz, seq_len=seq_len
+    )
+
+    for b, n in enumerate(lens):
+        rows = slice(b * seq_len, b * seq_len + n)
+        ref = F.scaled_dot_product_attention(
+            *(t[rows].transpose(0, 1).float() for t in (q, k, v))
+        ).transpose(0, 1)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(out[rows].float(), ref, atol=2e-2, rtol=2e-2)
+        assert (out[b * seq_len + n : (b + 1) * seq_len] == 0).all()
+
+
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     sys.exit(pytest.main([__file__]))
